newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crudes subdued, Brent talk fades.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crudes subdued, Brent talk fades.

text.p: The U.S. foreign crude scene was subdued on Thursday as buyers assessed first-half May activity in anticipation of further purchases, traders said.
"The market's been very quiet today," one Gulf Coast trader said.
Wednesday's talk of bringing North Sea Brent and Forties crude to the U.S. Gulf Coast faded amid ample Atlantic basin supplies.
Other North Sea grades from the Norwegian side, however, continued to flock to the Gulf Coast.
Two Gullfaks cargoes were recently sold, fetching discounts of around $1.10-15 a barrel to West Texas Intermediate/Cushing for April 23-27.
Oseberg was indicated around WTI minus 40-45 cents a barrel for mid-May arrival.
The May spread between WTI and Brent was around $1.55-60 a barrel, maintaining the open transatlantic arbitrage.
From Latin America, Colombia's sweet Cusiana crude was pegged at WTI minus $1.40-50 a barrel, up 10-20 cents from recent trades.
The uptick was attributed to softer Caribbean freight rates compared to last week, as well as thinner availabilities of similar sweet grades from the North Sea.
Equity producers had two Cusiana cargoes remaining for next month, one loading May 19-23 and other around May 17-21.
